title: Walking, age, and mortality
content: Pearl's Figure 4.2 models age as a confounder of the proposed effect of walking on mortality. The reported Honolulu study rates are source evidence, while the graph identifies age as an admissible back-door adjustment variable.

variables.name: Age
variables.content: Age influences both walking intensity and mortality risk.

variables.name: Walking
variables.content: Daily walking intensity is the proposed cause or treatment.

variables.name: Mortality
variables.content: Mortality over the study period is the outcome.

arrows.because: The source explains that younger men may be more willing to walk vigorously.
The source explains that younger men are also less likely to die.
This is the proposed causal effect investigated by the study.
